Plot Comparison Data

Source: R/f_comparison_plot.R
plotComparison.Rd

Produces a ggplot object from unrounded comparison data.

Usage

plotComparison(
  data,
  xParamName = NULL,
  yParamName = NULL,
  ...,
  groupParamName = NULL,
  categoryParamName = NULL,
  mainTitle = NULL,
  legendTitle = NULL,
  plotLineEnabled = TRUE,
  plotPointsEnabled = TRUE,
  pointBorder = 4,
  discreteXAxis = FALSE,
  mirrorModeEnabled = FALSE,
  legendPosition = "auto",
  shinyOptimization = FALSE,
  objects = NULL,
  yAxisSide = "auto",
  categoryLegendPosition = NULL,
  parameterLegendPosition = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A non-empty comparison data frame, a TrialComparison, or its summary.

xParamName, yParamName

Optional axis columns, selected by getComparisonPlotParameters() when omitted. yParamName may be a vector of distinct numeric columns.

...

Reserved for future extensions.

groupParamName

Optional grouping column, mapped to colour when categories are also present.

categoryParamName

Optional character vector of category columns. Multiple columns define their joint combinations. NULL selects categories automatically; NA_character_ or character(0) disables categories.

mainTitle

Plot title. When omitted, generated from the original objects using the same title as print and summary. Supply NULL or NA to hide it.

legendTitle

Category/group legend title. When omitted, object identifiers use Design, Calculation, Simulation, or a combination derived from the original objects or comparison metadata. Other categories use their parameter captions. With multiple y parameters and no categories, the title is Parameter. Explicit titles, including NULL to hide titles, take precedence.

plotLineEnabled, plotPointsEnabled

Whether to show lines and points.

pointBorder

Point border style, as used by rpact plots.

discreteXAxis

Whether numeric x ticks should use the observed values only.

mirrorModeEnabled

Whether to use fill categories without a legend.

legendPosition

Shared legend position. "auto" (default) uses the adaptive placement described below. Alternatively use rpact positions 1 (top left), 2 (centre left), 3 (bottom left), 4 (top right), 5 (centre right), 6 (bottom right), -1 (hidden), 0 (default position with square aspect), or a ggplot position name (none, left, right, bottom, top).

shinyOptimization

Whether to use compact sizing for Shiny displays.

objects

Optional original objects for role-aware selection with a data frame, as in getComparisonPlotParameters().

yAxisSide

Axis assignment: "auto" (default), "left", or "right". Supply one value for all y parameters, a vector in their order, or a named vector assigning individual parameters. Unspecified named entries remain automatic. The same argument is accepted by plotComparison().

categoryLegendPosition, parameterLegendPosition

Optional separate positions for category/group and y-parameter legends, using the same values as legendPosition. NULL inherits the shared setting. With both guides present, shared automatic positioning uses the adaptive layout described below. Explicit positions override this layout; two explicit inside positions may place the guides independently. A shared hidden legend remains hidden.

Value

A ggplot object, which can be customized with ggplot2 layers.

Details

Selection is delegated to getComparisonPlotParameters(). If its message is non-NULL, plotting raises an error using that text. Applications can call the selector first to display choices and messages without creating a plot. Multiple category columns are combined into a discrete colour (or fill when an explicit group is present or mirror mode is enabled). Legend labels show category values in the supplied column order, separated by ' / '. Every observed combination remains distinct, including missing values and values containing separators. Category columns must be distinct valid column names. More than nine colour groups use a hue palette instead of the limited Set1 palette, so every combination receives a colour. Categories and groups jointly identify lines. Without either, objectNumber (or designNumber) identifies separate objects. Stages are separated unless used as an axis. Select categories explicitly to compare results across objects along a parameter axis.

Multiple y parameters are drawn as separate series, identified by line type and point shape. These styles cycle for larger selections and can be replaced with ggplot2 scales. Categories and groups remain independent of the parameter identity. All axis labels and parameter legends use the rpact parameter captions with the original object context when available, falling back to technical names for unknown parameters. This also applies to a single y parameter. With two y axes, right-axis values are transformed onto the left plotting scale and the right axis displays the exact inverse transformation, retaining original units. Raw values and original columns remain in the long plot data; the caller's data are not modified. Explicitly placing all parameters on the right uses one primary axis on the right. Parameters assigned to the same side always share that scale.

For multiple y parameters with category/group legends, legendPosition = "auto" prefers horizontal category entries below the x-axis and a separate vertical parameter legend automatically placed inside. Category entries wrap into rows according to measured guide and panel dimensions. If the parameter legend takes too much inside space or covers more data, the alternative layout places it vertically below the panel and positions the category legend inside. Layout changes and label wrapping precede font reductions, which are limited to ten percent. If neither inside layout fits, both guides are placed below the panel. Very large legends still require a larger graphics device or an explicit layout. Explicit shared positions, such as "bottom", continue to apply to both guides unless a separate position is supplied. With only one guide, the common rpact positioning rules apply. Automatic inside placement scores points and line segments in panel coordinates, including secondary-axis scaling. This is a heuristic using the current device (seven inches square if none is open); resizing or exporting to another size may require recreating the plot.

Interactive converters must preserve the secondary-axis transformation. A plain plotly::ggplotly() conversion may omit the right axis and display transformed hover values. getComparisonPlotParameters() exposes the side assignments and transformation for application-specific adapters.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data <- getComparisonData(list(getDesignFixed(), getDesignGroupSequential()))
plotComparison(data, "stages", "criticalValues", plotLineEnabled = FALSE)
plotComparison(data, "stages", "criticalValues",
    categoryParamName = c("objectType", "sided"), plotLineEnabled = FALSE)
performance <- as.data.frame(getPowerAndAverageSampleNumber(
    getDesignGroupSequential(kMax = 3), nMax = 100))
plotComparison(performance, "theta",
    c("averageSampleNumber", "overallEarlyStop", "calculatedPower"),
    yAxisSide = c(averageSampleNumber = "left",
        overallEarlyStop = "right", calculatedPower = "right"),
    plotPointsEnabled = FALSE)
plotComparison(data, "stages", c("criticalValues", "stageLevels"),
    categoryLegendPosition = "auto", parameterLegendPosition = "bottom")
} # }
